newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr National stock dives, gp says misplaced.
newsitem.headline: Cr National stock dives, gp says misplaced.

text.p: Credit National shares tumbled on Wednesday after a newspaper report focusing on a risk of downgrades by rating agencies.
The stock lost five percent in afternoon trading but crept back to 237 francs, down 3.27 percent, at 1425 GMT.

But chairman Emmanuel Rodocanachi said the share's recent poor performance was due to a misunderstanding in the markets and that the strength of the new group emerging from Credit National's takeover of BFCE bank had been underrated.
Asked if he saw prospects for a reversal of the share trend, he replied: "Yes if the market took account of the real strength of the group".
"There's a misunderstanding in the market, it is a shame that it has not been possible to see the wood for the trees," he said in an interview with Reuters.

Rodocanachi said the group's announcement in late September of a fall into first-half loss had been preceded very closely by an unfavourable chain of events including optimistic forecasts by several analysts at a time when the firm had just also just discovered it would have to provision heavily for one specific capital investment project.

"There's no reason to have any doubt about our stability," he said, adding that the market also focused on weakness in medium- and long-term financing when this now accounted for 17 percent of a much more broadly-based business.

The group made a net attributable loss of 112 million francs in the first half after announcing a provision of 500 million francs for restructuring in the wake of the BFCE acquisition and said it would have made a profit of about 100 million if it had not had to make this provision.

The group is negotiating with staff about slimming the joint Credit National/BFCE workforce by the equivalent of some 600 jobs through working time changes and voluntary departures and Rodocanachi said he hoped for an agreement by around January.
Failing an agreement, the company would have to enact its restructuring plans unilaterally from about March or April.

Rodocanachi repeated his expectations that the group result should get "back above zero" in 1996 and that there would be a dividend. He said it was "far too early" to estimate the level of the payout.

Rodocanachi also stressed that the change in the group's legal status from that of a specialised financial institution to that of a commercial bank like others in the AFB French bank association would help the group.

Rating agencies are currently assessing their views on Credit National. The IBCA agency said after the first-half results it had put the group's short term A1 and long term A notes on creditwatch with negative implications.

A report in La Tribune daily newspaper on Monday centred on the possibility of a downgrading by Standard & Poors, after which the share tumbled to as low as 232.2 francs, close to its year low of 231.1 francs. It closed down 3.67 percent at 236.
